articles.title: Antrophic's IPO beats records
articles.heading: Nordic Alert
articles.fulltext:
Global key stories
European stock markets were mostly in the red yesterday, and pessimism persisted in the US, where the S&P 500 continued down for the fifth consecutive day after renewed declines in Nvidia. The tech-heavy Nasdaq went against the tide ahead of Antrophic's debut on the stock market. The introduction has been seen as a test of the market's continued interest in AI. It turned out that Antrophic had no trouble finding buyers. The IPO broke Spacex's previous record as the largest ever, and the company is now valued at about 1500 billion USD. Speaking of Spacex, Musk says in an interview with the New York Times that he is not MAGA, that he regrets the large sums (about 400 million USD) he invested in the Republicans ahead of the Texas election, and that he believes shared government could be good for the US. Perhaps this is the first of several outstretched hands from American tech companies now that the balance of power has shifted? In Asia, stock markets are mostly lower today, while futures are up for both the US, especially Nasdaq, and Europe.
The oil price
 has traded relatively steadily overnight at 92 USD/barrel after reports in the New York Times that President Trump is considering new attacks on Iran, along with Israel. US 10-year yields rose by some bp in connection with the release of the Fed's meeting minutes but have otherwise remained stable, and the market continues to discount just over three more hikes from the Fed. The dollar is trading below 1.10 against the euro. Weak labor market data has put pressure on AUD on expectations that the Australian central bank, RBA, is done hiking, which is also our view.
Not just Waller wanting to raise by 50 basis points. 
 The minutes from the October meeting showed that a couple of Fed members discussed the possibility of a larger hike in the event of unfavorable inflation data. Fed Governor Christopher Waller, who scared the market a few weeks ago with his 50-point hike speech, is therefore not entirely alone in this view. Otherwise, the minutes showed that most members supported the decision to keep rates unchanged in October, but that almost all expected further tightening. Data since the October meeting has been strong, and Fed members sound increasingly hawkish. We continue to believe in a hike in December, but with the possibility of another step in March 2027. Read more 
here
. Waller was interviewed yesterday by CNBC and reiterated his calls for a 50-point hike in December as a way to shock the market but also said that the Fed could settle for a 25 basis point hike if it clearly indicated a further hike in January. This is contrary to Chairman Kevin Warsh's reluctance to provide forward guidance and can be seen as yet another step in Waller's attacks against the new communication strategy.
The world's eyes today are on the APEC meeting in Shenzhen 
and the historic meeting between President Trump, Xi, and Putin. Trump and Putin have met one-on-one ahead of the tripartite meeting, and Trump will do the same with Xi later today. Trump praised the good relationship with his friend Putin but said at the same time that he would not make a deal with Putin about Ukraine without Ukraine's participation.
Today's data calendar is thin
 and topped by Norges Bank's survey of inflation expectations, labour costs, and construction in the Eurozone, as well as, in the US, the Philadelphia Fed manufacturing index.
Nordic key stories
The Riksbank's executive board is being questioned
 in the Swedish Riksdag Finance Committee today. We will be watching for new clues about when the next hike will come and how Riksbank board members weigh the risk of inflation against the risk of the recovery stalling.

articles.title: Rusning efter Antrophics aktier
articles.heading: Morning Alert
articles.fulltext:
Internationellt
Det var mestadels röda siffror på börserna i Europa igår och pessimismen höll i sig i USA där S&P500 fortsatte ned för femte dagen i rad efter förnyade nedgångar i Nvidia. Tekniktunga Nasdaq gick mot strömmen inför AI-bolaget Antrophics debut på börsen. Introduktionen har setts som ett test på marknadens fortsatta intresse för AI. Det visade sig att Antrophic inte hade några problem att hitta köpare. Emissionen slog Spacex tidigare rekord som den största någonsin och bolaget värderas nu till ca 1500 mdr USD. Apropå Spacex säger Musk, i en intervju med New York Times, att han inte är MAGA, att han ångrar de stora summor (ca 400 mln USD) som han satsade på republikanerna inför valet i Texas och att han tror att ett delat styre kan vara bra för USA. Kanske är detta den första av flera utsträckta händer från amerikanska techbolag nu när maktförhållandena har skiftat? I Asien är börserna mestadels lägre idag medan terminerna pekar uppåt för både USA, särskilt Nasdaq, och Europa.
Oljepriset
 har handlats relativt stabilt under natten på 92 USD/fatet efter rapporter i New York Times att president Trump överväger nya attacker mot Iran, tillsammans med Israel. Amerikanska 10-årsräntor steg någon punkt i samband med Feds mötesprotokoll, men har i övrigt varit stabila, och marknaden fortsätter att diskontera ytterligare drygt tre höjningar från Fed. Dollarn handlas under 1,10 mot euron. Svaga arbetsmarknadsdata satte press på AUD på förväntningar om att det är färdighöjt från den australiska centralbanken, RBA, vilket även är vår syn.
Inte bara Waller som vill höja 50 punkter. 
Protokollet från oktobermötet visade att ett par Fed-ledamöter diskuterade möjligheten till ett större höjningssteg i oktober i händelse av ogynnsamma inflationsdata. Feds guvernör Christopher Waller, som skrämde upp marknaden häromveckan med sitt tal om 50-punktershöjning, är således inte helt ensam om denna åsikt. I övrigt visade protokollet att de flesta av ledamöterna stödde beslutet om oförändrad ränta i oktober men att nästan alla förväntade sig ytterligare åtstramning. Data sedan oktobermötet har varit starka och Fed-ledamöterna låter alltmer hökaktiga. Vi fortsätter att tro på en höjning i december, men med en möjlighet till ytterligare ett steg i mars 2027. Läs mer 
här
. Waller intervjuades igår av CNBC och upprepade då kraven på en 50-punktershöjning i december som ett sätt att chocka marknaden men sa också att Fed skulle kunna nöja sig med att höja 25 punkter om man tydligt indikerade en ytterligare höjning i januari. Detta är på tvärs mot ordförande Kevin Warsh’s ovilja att ge forward guidance och kan väl ses som ännu ett led i Wallers krypskytte mot den nya kommunikationsstrategin.
Världens ögon riktas idag mot APEC-mötet i Shenzen 
och det historiska mötet mellan president Trump, Xi och Putin. Trump och Putin har träffats på tu man hand inför trepartsmötet och Trump kommer att göra detsamma med Xi senare idag. Trump hyllade den goda relationen med sin vän Putin men sa samtidigt att han inte kommer att göra upp med Putin om Ukraina utan Ukrainas medverkan.
Dagens datakalender är tunn
 och toppas av Norges Banks undersökning av inflationsförväntningar i Norge, arbetskraftskostnader och byggande i Euroområdet, samt, i USA, industriindex för Philadelphia-området.
Sverige
Riksbankens direktion frågas ut
 i Riksdagens finansutskott idag. Vi kommer att hålla utkik efter nya ledtrådar kring när nästa höjning kommer och hur direktionsledamöterna väger risken för inflation mot risken för att återhämtningen kommer av sig.

articles.title: Almost all expected a further rate increase, a couple discussed a 50 bp move
articles.heading: Fed minutes
articles.fulltext:
The minutes from the October 27-28 meeting showed that most members supported the decision to hold rates steady but that almost all expected that the Fed would raise rates further. A couple of members discussed a larger 50 bp move. Strong data since the meeting is likely to have strengthened the case for further tightening and we see it as likely that members will indicate another rate increase in their projections in December. We stick to our view of one more rate increase in December but risks are clearly skewed for another increase, possibly in March. 
Key points
Most members supported unchanged rate in October
Close call for a few members
Almost all expected the Fed to raise rates further
Waller not alone in discussing 50 bp move
We expect a rate increase in December and possibly also in March 
Unchanged rates was a close call for a few members 
The minutes from the October 27-28 meeting shows that most members supported the decision to hold rates steady, awaiting more information and (according to a couple of members) to give businesses and households time to adjust to higher interest rates. However, it was a close call for a few participants, while some favoured a rate increase. Two members, Lisa Cook and Beth Hammack, voted to raise rates by 25 bp at the October meeting and the language in the minutes suggest that their views were shared by other members. However, a few who favoured a rate increase would, according to the minutes, have supported unchanged rates provided it was “clearly understood” by market participants that further tightening was likely. This could be a sign that some members are critical against Chair Warsh’s new communication policy, including his resistance to forward guidance. Judging from his recent comments and speeches, Governor Christopher Waller is likely to be among those.
A couple saw a larger step as appropriate in case of unfavourable inflation data 
Almost all participants thought that the Fed would likely have to raise its policy rate further. The minutes also shows that the possibility of a larger 50 bp hike at the December meeting was discussed at the meeting and that “a couple” believed it could be appropriate if incoming inflation data were “unfavorable”. Thus, Governor Waller is not alone in thinking that the Fed may be forced to move in larger steps though in the minority. We also note that “some” participants thought market-implied tightening expectations were broadly consistent with their own views of an appropriate policy path. At the time of the meeting, markets were pricing a high probability for a December rate increase and two more by the summer of 2027.
Most members expected inflation to return to target over time
The minutes did otherwise not contain much news. Inflation was expected to remain elevated in the near term, but most members expected it to return to the target over time, reflecting waning effects of tariffs, a reduction in the contribution from energy and a moderation of price pressures from the AI buildout. At the same time, the “vast majority” saw upside risks to this outlook. This suggests that tighter policy could be seen as a precautionary step by the Fed rather than as necessary.
AI build-out remains in focus for the Fed
Much of the discussion focused on the risks from the AI buildout for inflation. The labour market was seen as stable and close to maximum employment, though many saw signs of a modest tightening. A majority noted that financial conditions had tightened since the September meeting – as pointed out by Chair Kevin Warsh at the press conference – though several members believed that financial conditions remained supportive of growth. Economic activity was generally seen as strong, reflecting resilient household spending and robust investment.
Strong support for another rate increase in December, split thereafter
We view the minutes as strongly supportive of another rate increase in December, but with members more split about the path thereafter. The discussion in the October minutes is, however, outdated since it took place before recent stronger data for both the labour market (the higher-than-expected payroll growth in October) and for CPI inflation (which surprised on the upside in October and with relatively broad-based upside surprises). Recent comments from Fed members have in general been hawkish though Waller has been alone in discussing 50bp steps. 
We expect another rate increase in December and possibly also in March
FOMC members will not get much more data ahead of the December 8-9 FOMC meeting. There will be one more employment report, for November, released on 4 December, while November CPI will only be released the day after the FOMC meeting. Developments in financial conditions, including equities, and geopolitical developments in the Middle East, may also affect the decision. But barring any large surprises we expect the Fed to raise rates by another 25 bp at the December meeting. Members will also release new projections for the economy and rates, and we see it as likely that these will signal a large probability for at least one more rate increase in 2027, given that many members are now talking about further rate increases (in plural), though most seem to prefer a gradual pace rather than a larger 50 bp move. We continue to expect the Fed to raise rates again in December and possibly also in March 2027. Markets continue to price a small probability of a larger increase in December (27 bp) and at least two more rate increases until summer (81 bp by September).

articles.title: Nvidia beats expectations - Fed minutes tonight
articles.heading: Nordic Alert
articles.fulltext:
Global key stories
Stock market indices in both Europe and the U.S. continued to decline yesterday, with the tech sector under pressure and new concerns about cybersecurity emerging after 
CNN reported
 network problems at the U.S. National Security Agency (NSA). The Euro Stoxx fell just over 2 percent and the S&P 500 by 1 percent, while long-term yields edged lower. The dollar weakened slightly against several other major currencies, but the Swedish krona fared worse, losing ground against all other G10 currencies. Nvidia’s after-close quarterly report yesterday 
beat expectations
, forecasting a revenue growth of 75 percent in 2028, which appears to be easing some of the concerns surrounding the AI sector for the time being. Asian stock markets are rising this morning, and futures point to a slightly positive opening in the U.S. and a flat opening in Europe. 
Today:
 A slew of central bank speeches are on today's agenda, including remarks by the ECB’s Lagarde and the Riksbank’s Hjelm, as well as UK inflation data and the Fed minutes tonight. Geopolitics is also likely to draw attention as Trump, Xi, and Putin, among others, gather at the APEC meeting in Shenzhen. The focus will be particularly on trade policy, AI, and geopolitical relations between the U.S. and China.
Fed minutes are in the spotlight tonight
. Incoming data continues to signal a resilient U.S. economy with elevated inflationary pressures, and the market is pricing in nearly 80 basis points higher policy rates by September of next year - almost 40 basis points more than just two weeks ago. Higher energy prices have slowed the decline in overall inflation and increased the risk of indirect effects through, for example, transportation costs. We see some signs that goods inflation is on the rise, while high mortgage rates are creating barriers in the housing market and risk leading to larger rent increases. While wage inflation continues to moderate, uncertainty surrounding the inflation outlook has increased and is putting pressure on the Fed.
UK core inflation is expected to ease slightly. 
The Bank of England raised its inflation forecast markedly at its most recent meeting, driven mainly by direct and indirect effects of high energy prices. We do not see support for such a sharp rise in short-term indicators and believe that the BoE is overestimating inflationary pressures going forward. Since the last meeting, the market has priced in a significantly tighter monetary policy over the coming year. 
While the risks are certainly on the upside for 
our forecast
 of a final interest rate hike in February, we also believe that the market is anticipating an overly aggressive tightening.
Nordic key stories
Swedish government negotiations continue
. After the Centre Party decided to move forward with the Social Democrats’ government government alternative, the deadlock over the Left Party’s demands for cabinet posts remains, and a final solution does not appear to be within reach. The exploratory talks are now on hold for a week to give the parties room for further negotiations, and all parties will then be summoned to a new round of talks with the Speaker next week. For the market, direct effects are very limited, but uncertainty surrounding economic policy remains. The Speaker said yesterday that he expects either a government or a new, extraordinary election to be announced before Christmas and New Year’s.

articles.title: Nvidia slår förväntningarna - Fed-protokoll i kväll
articles.heading: Morning Alert
articles.fulltext:
Internationellt
Börsindex i både Europa och USA fortsatte ned under gårdagen, med tech-sektorn under press och nya orosmoln kring cybersäkerhet efter att 
CNN rapporterat
 om nätverksproblem hos amerikanska säkerhetstjänsten NSA (National Security Authority). Eurostoxx sjönk drygt 2 procent och S&P500 med runt 1 procent samtidigt som långa räntor backade marginellt. Dollarn försvagades något mot flera andra stora valutor, men kronan hade det tuffare och tappade mark mot samtliga övriga G10-valutor. Nvidias 
oväntat starka kvartalsrapport
, där företaget bland annat ser intäktstillväxt på 75 procent under 2028, ser ut att dämpa lite av oron kring AI-sektorn för stunden – asiatiska börser stiger under morgonen och terminsprissättningen tyder på svagt positiv öppning i USA och runt nollan i Europa.
Idag:
Under dagen väntar bland annat en lång rad centralbankstal (bland annat av ECB:s Lagarde och Riksbankens Hjelm), brittisk inflation och Fed-protokoll.
Även geopolitiken lär få uppmärksamhet när bland annat Trump, Xi och Putin samlas på APEC-möte i Shenzhen. Fokus riktas inte minst mot handelspolitiken, AI och de geopolitiska relationerna mellan USA och Kina.
Fed-protokoll i fokus i kväll.
 Inkommande statistik fortsätter att signalera en motståndskraftig amerikansk ekonomi med förhöjt inflationstryck, och marknaden prissätter nära 80 räntepunkter högre styrränta fram till september nästa år, nästan 40 punkter mer än för bara två veckor sedan. Högre energipriser har bromsat nedgången i totalinflationen och ökat risken för indirekta effekter via exempelvis transportkostnader. Vi ser vissa tecken på att varuinflationen är på väg upp samtidigt som höga bolåneräntor skapar låsningar på bostadsmarknaden och riskerar att leda till större hyresökningar. Löneinflationen fortsätter visserligen att dämpas, men osäkerheten kring inflationsutsikterna har ökat och sätter press på Fed.
Brittisk kärninflation väntas sakta in något.
 Bank of England höjde inflationsprognosen kraftigt vid det senaste mötet, huvudsakligen drivet av direkta och indirekta effekter av höga energipriser. Vi tycker oss inte riktigt se stöd för en så skarp uppgång i kortsiktiga indikatorer och tror att BoE överskattar inflationstrycket framöver. Marknaden har sedan det senaste mötet prisat in en betydligt stramare penningpolitik det kommande året. Riskerna ligger visserligen på uppsidan för 
vår prognos
 om en sista räntehöjning i februari, men vi bedömer samtidigt att marknaden räknar med alltför aggressiv åtstramning.
Sverige
Regeringsförhandlingarna fortsätter.
 Efter att Centerpartiet valt att gå vidare med Socialdemokraternas regeringsunderlag kvarstår låsningen kring Vänsterpartiets krav på ministerposter, och någon slutlig lösning tycks inte vara inom räckhåll. Sonderingsprocessen pausas nu i en vecka för att ge partierna utrymme för fortsatta förhandlingar, och samtliga partier kommer därefter att kallas till en ny talmansrunda nästa vecka. För marknaden är de direkta effekterna mycket begränsade men osäkerheten kring den ekonomiska politiken består. Talmannen meddelade igår att han förväntar sig att en regering, eller ett extraval, har tillkännagivits före jul och nyår.
Lyssningstips!
Svensk ekonomi under luppen.
 Högre räntor, energipriser som skjuter i höjden och ännu ingen regering på plats. Samtidigt växer svensk ekonomi över trend och prognosen är att kronan kommer att stärkas under 2027. Men varför påverkar högre oljepriser Sverige och hur kommer det sig att räntehöjningar slår hårdare här än i övriga Europa? Allt detta, och mycket, mycket mer, diskuterar undertecknad och Olle Holmgren med SEB:s chefsekonom Jens Magnusson i 
det senaste avsnittet av Makropodd
.

articles.title: AI concerns persist – update on Swedish government formation
articles.heading: Nordic Alert
articles.fulltext:
Global key stories
AI concerns weighed on equities and supported the dollar
. Markets remained unsettled by AI concerns yesterday. The Nasdaq fell 2.5% and the S&P 500 lost 1.9%. European equities also declined, but losses were considerably smaller (Euro Stoxx 50 −0.6%). The immediate focus is on Nvidia’s earnings tonight and Anthropic’s planned IPO later this week. Nvidia has generated plenty of headlines in recent days, and its shares fell more than 4% yesterday. The US 10-year Treasury yield edged lower while the dollar continued to strengthen. Brent crude fell to around USD 92 per barrel, down 4% from Friday. A recovery in Middle Eastern exports and the International Energy Agency’s (IEA) forecast of a supply surplus in Q4 outweighed persistent security risks around the Strait of Hormuz. According to media reports, a third US aircraft carrier has now arrived in the Middle East, somewhat at odds with President Trump’s recent statements that the Iran war is “effectively” over.
Yesterday, Fed Chair Warsh delivered opening remarks at a conference in San Francisco organised by the Federal Reserve’s task force on productivity and jobs. Perhaps unsurprisingly, he focused on both the opportunities offered by AI (higher productivity and growth) and the risks (higher unemployment and falling equity markets). Warsh also presented three scenarios with different implications for growth and employment. His remarks offered little new guidance on the near-term interest rate outlook.
Most Asian equity markets are lower. Overnight, the White House announced further restrictions on China’s access to advanced AI chips from companies such as Nvidia. The rules restrict shipments to data centres in countries including Thailand, Malaysia and Brazil. Chinese companies have used data centres in these countries to access computing capacity to train AI models. Ahead of today’s market openings, US equity futures are slightly higher, while European futures are lower.
New Investment Outlook.
 Our colleagues at SEB Asset Management and Investments present their views on market conditions in today’s 
Investment Outlook.
 Strong corporate earnings and continued economic expansion support equities. Meanwhile, the focus of the AI buildout is shifting from the pace of investment to profitability, while high energy prices and inflation risks create uncertainty. Broad diversification is becoming increasingly important. With most of the rise in yields likely behind us, bonds have a clearer role as both a source of returns and a portfolio risk diversifier.
EU defence ministers meet in Brussels today
 to discuss the EU’s relationship with China from a defence and security perspective, support for Ukraine and transatlantic security. Several Fed and ECB officials are also scheduled to speak. The data calendar contains no major macroeconomic releases, but October US retail sales and industrial production figures will provide useful indications of whether growth remains robust.
Nordic key stories
65 days after the Swedish election
, Moderate Party leader Ulf Kristersson will today report to the Speaker on his ongoing efforts to form a government. The Speaker can then either give another candidate an opportunity to form a government or put Kristersson forward for a parliamentary vote as prime minister. If Kristersson is voted down, only one further vote remains before an extraordinary election is triggered.

articles.title: AI-oron håller i sig - nytt besked om regeringsbildningen
articles.heading: Morning Alert
articles.fulltext:
Internationellt
AI-oro pressade börserna och stärkte dollarn
. Gårdagen präglades av fortsatt AI-oro. Nasdaq föll med 2,5% och S&P 500 med 1,9%. Även Europabörserna backade, men nedgångarna var betydligt mindre (Euro Stoxx 50 -0,6%). Fokus i närtid ligger på Nvidias rapport ikväll och Anthropics planerade börsintroduktion senare i veckan. Rubrikerna kring Nvidia har varit många de senaste dagarna och i går föll aktien med över 4%. USA:s tioårsränta sjönk något samtidigt som dollarn fortsatte att stärkas. Oljepriset (Brent) föll till runt 92 dollar per fat, en minskning med 4% jämfört med i fredags. En återhämning i exporten från Mellanöstern och Internationella energiorganets (IEA) prognos om ett utbudsöverskott under fjärde kvartalet vägde tyngre än fortsatta säkerhetsrisker kring Hormuzsundet. Enligt medieuppgifter har nu ett tredje amerikanskt hangarfartyg anlänt till Mellanöstern, vilket går lite stick i stäv med President Trumps senaste uttalanden om att Irankriget ”i praktiken” är över.
Igår höll Fed-chefen Warsh ett inledningstal vid en konferens i San Francisco, anordnad av Federal Reserves arbetsgrupp för produktivitet och sysselsättning. Kanske inte så förvånande att centralbankschefen var fokuserad på såväl möjligheterna med AI (högre produktivitet och tillväxt) som riskerna (högre arbetslöshet och börsfall). Warsh presenterade även tre scenarier med olika effekter på tillväxt och sysselsättning. Talet gav egentligen inga nya signaler om ränteläget i närtid.
I Asien backar de flesta börserna. Vita huset meddelade i natt att man ytterligare kommer att begränsa Kinas tillgång till avancerade AI-chip från företag som exempelvis Nvidia. Reglerna begränsar leveranser till datacenter i bland annat Thailand, Malaysia och Brasilien. Kinesiska företag har använt datacenter i dessa länder för att få tillgång till beräkningskapacitet för att träna AI-modeller. Inför dagens öppningar är terminerna svagt upp i USA och ned i Europa.
Ny Investment Outlook. 
Våra kollegor på SEB Asset Management och Investments redogör för sin syn på marknadsläget i dagens 
Investment Outlook
. Starka företagsvinster och fortsatt ekonomisk expansion ger stöd åt aktiemarknaden. Samtidigt skiftar fokus i AI-utbyggnaden från investeringstakt till lönsamhet, medan höga energipriser och inflationsrisker skapar osäkerhet. Bred riskspridning blir allt viktigare. Att större delen av ränteuppgången bör ligga bakom oss ger obligationer en tydligare roll som både avkastningskälla och riskdämpare i portföljen.
Idag möts EU:s försvarsministrar i Bryssel 
för att diskutera EU:s relation med Kina ur ett försvars- och säkerhetsperspektiv, stöd till Ukraina och transatlantisk säkerhet. Vi får även en rad tal från olika Fed- och ECB-ledamöter. Datakalendern innehåller inga tunga makrodata men oktobersiffrorna för amerikansk detaljhandel och industriproduktionen blir intressanta för att se om tillväxten fortsätter att vara robust.
Sverige
65 dagar efter valet ska
 Moderaternas Ulf Kristersson idag redovisa sitt pågående sonderingsuppdrag för talmannen. Talmannen kan då välja att antingen ge en annan kandidat möjlighet att bilda regering eller hålla en statsministeromröstning om Kristersson. Skulle Kristersson röstas ned återstår bara en till omröstning innan det blir extraval.

articles.title: Are higher rates finally biting?
articles.heading: Norway 360
articles.fulltext:
Norway 360 – Weekly Market (Re)View Norway 360 provides you with a quick and broad overview of Norwegian macro, rates and FX. 
*** See attachment for full report ***
Macro highlights (I): Is Norges Bank’s policy restrictive enough?  
Households feel the squeeze: 
Having reversed last year’s rate cuts, the current rate level is clearly weighing on household demand. Consumer confidence has plunged, household consumption has been surprisingly weak, and households’ savings intentions have reached record highs.
Housing market loses momentum:
The housing market is also losing momentum, with transaction times rising in the rate-sensitive Oslo market. Residential construction remains deeply depressed, while anecdotal evidence points to rising bankruptcies across the construction sector.
Monetary tightening is taking effect:
With monetary policy already restrictive and signs of cooling demand emerging, further hikes risk weakening the economy more than improving the long-term inflation outlook. We therefore see little scope for further tightening unless inflation prospects deteriorate materially.
Macro highlights (II): Nordic Outlook Update  
We have revised our forecast for mainland GDP growth this year down after a subdued H1 2026
.
Household 
consumption was particularly weak, mainly driven by temporary factors. 
S
entiment 
indicators point to broadly stable growth momentum towards year-end.
Recovering household consumption, supported by real wage gains and low unemployment will increasingly drive growth going forward. Improving consumption outlook in 2027 coupled with disinflation and normalization of borrowing costs will lift growth to 1.2%.
CPI-ATE inflation eased over summer but remains elevated. The outlook is mixed, with 
high wage
 costs sustaining services inflation while a stronger NOK dampens imported goods prices. We see upside risks to Norges Bank’s near-term forecast, but expect a faster decline in 2027, bringing inflation closer to target in early 2028.
We project that the policy rate has peaked but risks are skewed to the upside in the near term as Norges Bank has signaled a readiness to act if the inflation outlook deteriorates materially. Gradually lower inflation paves way for policy normalization starting in late 2027. We expect a policy rate of 3.75 per cent by end-2028, which is in the upper-end of Norges Bank’s neutral nominal rate band.
Rates highlights: Front-end view - we still prefer the NOK ‘FRA fly’  
Our main view remains that the NOK FRA curve should have more potential to invert (Jun27/Jun28) 
– a catalyst would obviously be a global disinflation impulse from the energy complex. 
We have been pairing this flattener view with a front micro steepener (Mar27/Jun27) 
as a ‘hedge’ on continued rates sell-off and that central banks may have to do more.
Norway like Australia sticks out in a G10 comparison as the market is pricing limited further upside in the front given already high policy rate levels, while cumulatively discounting more rate cuts further out. However, 
Norway is 
lagging behind
 as the market discounts more curve inversion into 2028 in Australia.
Historically, the NOK 3rd/7th FRA curve has inverted between 75-90bps when the market has speculated that Norges Bank is nearing a policy rate peak. This suggests that the Jun27/Jun28 FRA curve 
has potential to at least flatten another 60bps
.
An alternative expression for the Jun27/Jun28 flattener would be a NOK 2s10s steepener in fwd space
. Comparing current steepness with pricing in the front, the curve is not deviating too much from what a simple regression suggests. However, a further move closer to the 1 standard deviation line would make this an attractive alternative implementation.
FX highlights: Oil rather than gas taking over as marginal NOK-driver  
Oil has replaced gas as the marginal energy driver of NOK. The larger oil move in early November reflected a sharper unwinding of the Hormuz/Middle East risk premium as prospects for diplomacy improved and the market refocused on a potentially sizeable oil surplus. European gas remained better supported by winter inventories, restocking and weather risks, limiting its decline.
Combined with softer carry appetite, the larger oil move has reinforced NOK weakness and increased the importance of broader risk factors.
Hence, NOK/SEK continues to track the broader energy complex. While model attribution has recently shifted from gas towards oil, the two energy prices remain closely correlated. The distinction between oil and gas is therefore less important than the underlying message: energy remains the key directional driver of NOK/SEK.
Upcoming data & events:
Thursday’s inflation expectations survey will be closely watched, particularly business leaders’ expectations, which may offer valuable insight into domestic inflation prospects given firms’ price-setting role. Social partners wage growth expectations will also be in focus, with recent indications suggesting easing upward pressure on wages.

articles.title: Government formation talks continue in Sweden
articles.heading: Nordic Alert
articles.fulltext:
Global key stories
After a month of mostly falling bond yields, the trend finally reversed.
 A strong US labour market, slightly higher US inflation and hawkish comments from Fed officials over the past week caused more than half of the decline in the US 10-year Treasury yield during October to be reversed. European yields have followed suit – led by France – while expectations of further rate hikes from the Fed and ECB have increased. The prospect of central banks continuing to push interest rates higher from levels that already appear unsustainable in many countries, given high public debt, looks like a risky gamble. Higher rates will primarily hit US households and the already very weak housing market, while the impact on the AI investments driving US growth is probably negligible. The fact that parts of the Fed, which has historically almost always been forward-looking and focused on downside risks to growth even when actual inflation has deviated from target, now appear to have shifted towards scrutinising tenths of a percentage point in inflation is worrying for longer-term economic stability.
Equity markets continue to take rising bond yields relatively calmly.
 US equities recovered much of a sharp decline on Friday evening, although the S&P 500 still closed 0.4% lower. Nvidia continued to slide (falling almost 5% at one point), but recovered somewhat to close down 2%. Since its peak in early October, Nvidia has fallen 33%. According to the Financial Times, efforts are under way to persuade Nvidia's board to reinstate the recently ousted Jensen Huang as CEO. Asian equity markets are mostly lower, with the largest declines in Korea and Taiwan. US equity futures point to losses of a few tenths of a percentage point, while European futures are unchanged..
The minutes from the Fed's late-October rate decision
, when the Fed voted to leave rates unchanged with two dissenting votes, will be one of the highlights of an otherwise relatively light week for economic data. However, the summit between Trump, Xi and Putin on the sidelines of the APEC meeting in China is likely to attract even more attention. Negotiations on a nuclear agreement are the main purpose of the meeting, but the wars in Iran and Ukraine, along with trade policy, are also very likely to feature on the agenda. Anthropic's IPO, expected to be one of the largest ever, is another highlight. The plan is to set the IPO price on Wednesday, with trading in the shares beginning on Thursday.
Nordic key stories
A relatively quiet week for Swedish economic data,
 with money market inflation expectations today and labour market data on Friday. Developments in the labour market are certainly of great interest, but the Labour Force Survey (LFS) is too volatile to draw firm conclusions from individual monthly figures. We maintain our view that the Riksbank is too optimistic about the labour market. Both alternative measures of employment and various indicators support our assessment.
In Sweden Government formation talks continue. 
The Centre Party continues to  back Magdalena Andersson’s (Social democrat) plan to form a government comprising the Social Democrats, the Centre Party and the Green Party, which would then negotiate policy with the Left Party. Andersson’s proposal, containing around 100 policy points, will form the basis for these negotiations. However, the Left Party insists that it must also be part of the government, meaning that the proposed coalition still lacks sufficient support in parliament.
Ulf Kristersson (Moderate)
, who is due to report the outcome of his exploratory talks to the Speaker of Parliament tomorrow, will have to acknowledge that there is currently insufficient support for a centre-right government. The question is what the Speaker's next step will be. He will probably want to move towards a third parliamentary vote on a prime minister, but on which government? Another vote on Magdalena Andersson would, as things stand, merely confirm that the government formation process has made no progress, while Kristersson currently has no prospect of winning a vote.
In an opinion article, Magdalena Andersson argues that if the proposed coalition fails to secure sufficient support, a government bringing together the Moderate Party and the Social Democrats is the only solution.
 The Moderates have, however, rejected this option, at least with Andersson as prime minister. Two parliamentary votes on a prime minister remain, and speculation is growing that a snap election may become increasingly difficult to avoid.
 In Norway t
he upcoming Q4 Inflation Expectations Survey (Thu) 
will be important, especially business leaders’ inflation expectations as they lead domestic inflation. The Committee has previously highlighted elevated inflation expectation as a risk for inflation becoming entrenched. Social partners’ wage growth estimates will also be closely watched.

articles.title: Centern fortsätter stödja Magdalena Andersson
articles.heading: Morning Alert
articles.fulltext:
Internationellt
Efter en månad med mestadels fallande räntor 
höll det inte längre. Stark amerikansk arbetsmarknad, något högre USA-inflation och hökaktiga uttalanden från Fed-ledamöter under den senaste veckan gjorde att mer än hälften av nedgången i den amerikanska 10-årsräntan under oktober reverserades. Europa har dragits med – med Frankrike i spetsen – och förväntningarna på räntehöjningar från Fed och ECB har stigit. Att centralbankerna fortsätter att pressa upp räntorna från nivåer som på många håll redan verkar ohållbara, med tanke på den höga offentliga skuldsättningen, framstår som ett vågspel. Höga räntor kommer främst att drabba amerikanska hushåll och den redan mycket svaga bostadsmarknaden, medan effekterna på de AI-investeringar som driver tillväxten i USA antagligen är försumbara. Att delar av Fed, som historiskt nästan alltid varit framåtblickande och fokuserat på riskerna för tillväxten även när den faktiska inflationen avvikit från målet, nu verkar ha övergått till att analysera tiondelar i inflationen är oroande för den ekonomiska stabiliteten på sikt (enligt undertecknad).
Börserna fortsätter att ta de stigande räntorna med relativt stort lugn
. USA-börserna återhämtade stora delar av en kraftig nedgång under fredagskvällen, även om S&P 500 stängde ned 0,4%. Nvidia fortsatte nedåt (föll som mest med nästan 5%), men återhämtade sig delvis och stängde på minus 2%. Sedan toppnivån i början av oktober har Nvidia fallit med 33%. Enligt Financial Times pågår försök att övertyga Nvidias styrelse om att återta den nyss avsatte Jensen Huang som företagets vd. Börserna i Asien faller på de flesta håll, med störst nedgångar i Korea och Taiwan. Börsterminerna i USA pekar ned några tiondelar, medan de europeiska terminerna tyder på marginella uppgångar inledningsvis. 
 Oljepriset faller svagt trots rapporter om attacker i Persiska viken.
Fed-protokollet från räntebeskedet i slutet av oktober
, då Fed med två reservationer röstade för att lämna räntan oförändrad, är en av veckans höjdpunkter under en i övrigt ganska tunn statistikvecka. Toppmötet mellan Trump, Xi och Putin i samband med APEC-mötet i Kina kommer antagligen att stå ännu mer i fokus. Förhandlingar om ett kärnvapenavtal är mötets främsta syfte, men krigen i Iran och Ukraina och handelspolitik kommer med stor sannolikhet också att finnas på agendan. Börsintroduktionen av Anthropic, som bedöms bli en av de största någonsin, är ytterligare en höjdpunkt. Planen är att introduktionskursen fastställs på onsdag och att handeln med aktien inleds på torsdag.
Sverige
Även Sverige uppvisar en ganska tunn statistikvecka med penningmarknadens inflationsförväntningar idag och arbetsmarknadsdata på fredag i fokus
. Vad som händer på arbetsmarknaden är i och för sig högintressant, men AKU-statistiken är lite för volatil för att dra några större slutsatser av enskilda månadssiffror. Vi håller fast vid vår syn att Riksbanken är för optimistisk om arbetsmarknaden. Både alternativa mått på sysselsättningen och olika indikatorer stöder vår bild.
Regeringsförhandlingarna fortsätter. 
Centerpartiet ställer sig nu bakom Magdalena Anderssons plan att bilda en regering med Socialdemokraterna, Centerpartiet och Miljöpartiet, som sedan ska förhandla med Vänsterpartiet om politiken. Det förslag med cirka 100 punkter som Magdalena Andersson presenterat ska ligga till grund för förhandlingarna. Vänsterpartiet håller dock fast vid kravet att även partiet ska ingå i regeringen, vilket innebär att den föreslagna regeringen fortfarande saknar stöd i riksdagen.
Ulf Kristersson, som ska rapportera resultatet av sina sonderingar till talmannen imorgon,
 kommer att tvingas konstatera att stöd för en borgerlig regering saknas i nuläget. Frågan är vad talmannens nästa steg blir. Antagligen vill han få till en tredje statsministeromröstning, men om vilken regering? En ny omröstning om Magdalena Andersson skulle, som det ser ut nu, bara visa att regeringsbildningen inte kommit framåt alls, medan Ulf Kristersson i nuläget saknar möjligheter att vinna en omröstning.
Magdalena Andersson skriver i en debattartikel att om den nu föreslagna regeringen inte får stöd är en regering med både Moderaterna och Socialdemokraterna 
den enda lösningen. Moderaterna har dock avvisat den möjligheten, åtminstone med Andersson som statsminister. Två statsministeromröstningar återstår och allt fler spekulerar i att ett extraval kan bli svårt att undvika.

articles.title: Inflation and Fed minutes in the limelight
articles.heading: The Week Ahead
articles.fulltext:
Inflation and growth momentum remain in focus. In the US, Fed minutes and key activity data will provide further clues about the monetary policy outlook and whether strong growth momentum has continued into Q4. In the euro area, inflation data and business surveys will be closely watched for signs of energy-related price pressures and the impact of political uncertainty. In the Nordics, inflation expectations will be in focus, particularly in Norway, alongside Swedish unemployment data and ongoing government negotiations. 
US:
Fed minutes will be in focus for insights into the decision to leave rates unchanged at the October meeting and members’ views on the policy path ahead. Retail sales and industrial production will provide clues as to whether the strong growth momentum has continued into Q4. We will also get regional November sentiment surveys and housing market data. On Monday, Fed Chair Warsh will deliver opening remarks at the Federal Reserve’s productivity and jobs task force conference in San Francisco. Several other Fed members are also scheduled to speak during the week.
Euro area: 
We will scrutinise the final October HICP figures for further details on inflation developments. German PPI will also be of interest for signs of price pressures stemming from the war in the Middle East. France’s INSEE business survey may reflect the current political turmoil. Finally, the EU–UK summit will be closely watched, as well as other EU meetings.
Sweden:
Money market inflation expectations and unemployment are the only indicators this week. Government negotiations will continue and the Moderate leader Ulf Kristersson will report to the speaker of parliament on Tuesday.
Norway:
The upcoming Q4 Inflation Expectations Survey (Thu) will be important, especially business leaders’ inflation expectations as they lead domestic inflation. The Committee has previously highlighted elevated inflation expectation as a risk for inflation becoming entrenched. Social partners’ wage growth estimates will also be closely watched.

Global key stories
After admitting earlier this week that he had a relationship with a suspected Chinese spy, Jensen Huang 
resigned
 as CEO of Nvidia yesterday. This, along with higher Brent oil prices and interest rates, negatively impacted risk appetite with stock market declines in the US (S&P 500 -0.4%, Nasdaq -0.4%) although European stocks advanced (Euro Stoxx 50 +0.1%). The euro weakened against the dollar while the price of gold fell. In Asia, stock markets are opening upwards in Japan, down in China. 
Geopolitics
. President Trump said the U.S. 
doesn't need a deal
 with Iran and called on Vice President J.D. Vance to focus on corruption in opposition-controlled electoral districts. The president also threatened to 
double tariffs on Mexico
 if the country's government doesn't stop a group of about 1,500 migrants from walking toward the U.S. border. Volodymyr Zelenskyy, the President of Ukraine, stated that Starshield service has once again 
been limited
 for the country's armed forces and therefore makes its drone defense difficult. 
Statistics.
 Today, October's final inflation data for France, Spain and Poland will be released. In addition, the second estimate of euro area GDP and employment for the third quarter will be published. In the US, producer price inflation for October will be published, in Russia inflation and in Turkey, September's current account will be released.
